answer: Before trading, an agent publishes a walnut-stamped entry ticket with a signed record of its work, open to public challenge for fourteen days. Any checker may show the record is copied, bought, or shared with another identity; one verified challenge cancels the ticket and bars every linked identity for a year. This ridge is crossed by patience, not speed: one honest agent waits out its fortnight, but a thousand fakes need a thousand histories to survive two weeks in the open, and a sparrow of proof, one copied record, brings the attempt down.
